To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bioactivity-labels can be used for facilitated interpretation of principal component analysis of crude plant extracts, that this method was applied to Radix Astragalis, that the method revealed a new α-glucoside inhibitor, and that this inhibitor was structurally characterized.

bioactivity-labeled NMR spectroscopic data can be used to facilitate interpretation of the scores plot in principal component analysis and that a new α-glucoside inhibitor was identified in Radix Astragalus.
bioactivity-labeled PCA of crude extracts allows the identification of individual compounds contributing to the bioactivity of crude extracts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient strategy for the identification of new α-glucoside inhibitory constituents from Radix Astragalis.
the metabolomics of Radix Astragalus and the identification of new compounds with α-glucosides inhibitory activity.
the development of a novel approach to the identification of bioactive compounds in complex plant extracts by the use of bioactivity-labeling and multivariate statistical analysis of 1H NMR data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the bioactivity-labeling approach can facilitate the identification of the bioactive compounds in a complex extract, but it cannot substitute the traditional isolation and characterization of the individual constituents, and the bioactivity-labels are only indicative and should always be confirmed by other means.

the α-glucocidase inhibitory effect of Radix Astrgali is mainly due to isoflavones (genistein, formononetin, daidzein, and calycosin) and that the previously unreported long chain ferulates (1 and 2) contribute to the observed activity to a minor degree.
this study demonstrates the feasibility of bioactivity-labeling in 1H-NMRS for metabolomics investigations, and the identification of a new bioactive compound in Radix Astragalus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new approach for the identification of individual compounds in complex extracts, which contribute to the bioactivities observed for the extract as a whole.

we have developed a novel approach for metabolomics investigations, and we have identified and isolated a new α-glucoside inhibitor, linoleyl-ferulate, from Radix Astragalis, which is used for the treatment for diabetes in Chinese traditional medicine.
the bioactivity-labeled NMR approach is an excellent tool in metabolomics investigations, and the approach is particularly suitable for the discovery of bioactive constituents in crude extracts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bioactivity-labeled PCA can be used as an efficient tool to identify the most important constituents contributing to the bioactivity of a crude extract.
the use of bioactivity-labeled NMR spectroscopy in metabolomics studies can be a useful tool in identifying bioactive constituents in crude extracts.

the bioactivity-labeling approach is a useful and efficient way of identifying the individual compounds in crude plant extracts that contribute to the observed biological activity of the crude extracts.
